summary: Qian Lin works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Fudan University, the University of Bristol, and the University of Washington, where she earned her PhD under Collett Cox and Richard G. Salomon. She held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 2026).

Qiang Ning is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Supervised by Hung Wu and Irene Winter, he worked as a researcher at the Dunhuang Academy and taught at San Diego State University, Yale University, and the University of Michigan (attested 2004).

Qichao Liang (1873–1929) was a scholar in sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Youwei Kang (~1890–1898). He held posts at the Current Affairs Academy, the Translation Bureau, Nankai University, Tsinghua University, and the National Library of China.

Qing Duan (1953–2022) specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University and earned her PhD at the University of Hamburg (~1982–1986) under Ronald Eric Emmerick, later serving as professor at Peking University (~1987–2022).

Qingying Chen (1942–2022) worked in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Qinghai Nationalities University and Minzu University of China under Wang Yao. He taught at Qinghai Nationalities University and Minzu University before serving at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2006).
Qingzhi Zhu works in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He has held posts as a professor at Peking University (attested 2004) and the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
Qinni Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She studied at Fo Guang University, earning a Master of Arts under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
Qiwen Xiao specializes in Buddhist studies. She studied at Fo Guang University, where she earned a Master of Arts under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).

R. Balasubramanian (1929–2017) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under the traditional teacher Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri (attested 1988) and served as Director at the University of Madras from around 1978 to 1989.

R. D. Vadekar (1902–1986) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Shripad Krishna Belvalkar (attested 1929) and served as Professor of Sanskrit and Allied Languages at Fergusson College (attested 1958).
R. Gayathri works in Indology. She has been a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute studying under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

R. Gordon Wasson (1898–1986) worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the London School of Economics and Columbia University, later working in journalism and banking, including at J.P. Morgan & Co. (1934–1963) and the American Council of Learned Societies (1951).

R. H. Blyth (1898–1964) was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of London (~1919–1923) and held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1925–1940) and Kanazawa University (~1940–1941).

R. H. Tawney (1880–1962) was a historian who studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1899–1903). He held academic posts at the University of Glasgow (~1906–1908) and the London School of Economics (~1917–1949).
R. N. Gadre is an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Sir Parashurambhau College and at Savitribai Phule Pune University (both attested 1958).
R. P. Paranjpye (1876–1966) studied under Vaman Shivram Apte. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).

R. Ramanujachari worked in philosophy and Indology. He was Professor of Philosophy at Annamalai University (attested 1938–1940) and served as Editor of the Journal of the Annamalai University (attested 1950).

R. Sathyanarayana (1927–2020) was a scholar of Indology who completed a master's in chemistry at the University of Mysore. He taught at Sarada Vilas College (1949–1984) and served as President of the Indian Music Congress.
R. T. Vyas is an Indologist who served as General Editor for Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1988) and as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1993–1994).

R. Thangaswami Sarma (1924–2000) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Madras Sanskrit College and Annamalai University. He held positions at Presidency College, Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and Adyar Library and Research Centre (1994–2000).
